themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Surge
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about outdoor dining jumped to 10 THIS WEEK, up 789% from the 1.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.25), suggesting either rapid expansion of sidewalk seating or emerging quality-of-life conflicts in Greenpoint/Williamsburg.
evidence: 10 outdoor dining complaints this week vs. 1.1 weekly baseline (789% spike)
z-score of 5.25 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Spike is concentrated in current week only, suggesting rapid recent change
reporting_angles: Which restaurants have expanded outdoor seating recently? Interview affected residents about noise, odor, or pedestrian congestion.
Are post-pandemic outdoor dining licenses being renewed or expanded? Check DOE licensing data and cross-reference with complaint locations.

themes_detail.label: Street Signs Missing Citywide
themes_detail.summary: Missing street sign complaints spiked to 8 LAST WEEK, up 482% from the 1.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.73), indicating either new infrastructure damage or a lapse in maintenance affecting pedestrian and driver navigation.
evidence: 8 missing street sign complaints last week vs. 1.4 weekly baseline (482% spike)
z-score of 7.73 indicates highly significant statistical anomaly
Aligns with recurring CB budget request to improve traffic and pedestrian safety
reporting_angles: Obtain 311 complaint map to identify which intersections are affected. Visit and verify missing signs.
Contact DOT about recent sign removal projects or maintenance backlog—is this a known issue or unexpected failure?

themes_detail.label: Tree Request Explosion
themes_detail.summary: New tree requests surged to 3 THIS WEEK, up 2300% from the 0.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69), the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset, potentially signaling a community organizing moment or response to environmental concerns.
evidence: 3 new tree requests this week vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% spike)
z-score of 8.69 is the highest statistical anomaly across all complaint types
Spike is brand new (this week only), suggesting a sudden trigger or mobilization event
reporting_angles: Are residents responding to a specific environmental or beautification campaign? Interview requesters about motivation.
Check if a community group or elected official recently launched a tree-planting initiative in the district.

themes_detail.label: Emergency Response Team Complaints Rise
themes_detail.summary: Emergency Response Team complaints jumped to 8 LAST WEEK, up 113% from the 3.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.43), suggesting either increased NYPD or FDNY presence or quality-of-life conflicts escalating.
evidence: 8 ERT complaints last week vs. 3.8 weekly baseline (113% spike)
z-score of 6.43 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Recency is recent (last week) with possible connection to litter and public disorder spikes
reporting_angles: What types of 311 complaints are triggering ERT response? Cross-reference complaint location data.
Interview residents about visible police or emergency activity—are there specific blocks or times when ERT is present?

themes_detail.label: Public Sanitation Complaints Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket complaints spiked to 4 LAST WEEK, up 540% from the 0.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.4), and public urination complaints hit 3 TWO WEEKS AGO, up 380% from baseline (z-score: 3.41), suggesting a convergent public hygiene and homelessness-related trend that aligns with recurring CB budget requests for homeless services.
evidence: 4 litter basket complaints last week vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (540% spike)
3 public urination complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (380% spike)
Both spikes align with recurring CB request for 'services for the homeless'—suggests unmet systemic need
reporting_angles: Are there visible encampments or increased street homelessness in specific areas? Map complaints against known homeless services locations.
Interview sanitation workers, residents, and local business owners about conditions and trends—has open-air activity increased on specific blocks?
